Navy Midshipmen.oc: Drew Cronic, whose hiring the guide credits to Brian Newberry.
Navy Midshipmen.dc: Eric Lewis, promoted to coordinator, with Newberry himself returning to his roots as the defensive play-caller and P.J. Volker demoted to safeties coach.
Navy Midshipmen.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Navy Midshipmen.dc_status: New — the guide records the reshuffle, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Navy Midshipmen.play_caller: Changed on defense, and the guide treats the change as the story: sensing urgency, Newberry is returning to his roots as his own defensive play-caller, having demoted P.J. Volker to safeties coach and promoted Eric Lewis to coordinator.
Navy Midshipmen.offensive_scheme: Named. The guide describes Cronic's Wing-T modified triple option and says it gives opponents much to prepare for, recording the production shift precisely: 17.7 points per game in 2023, then 31.3 and 31.5 with 6.3 and 6.5 yards per play in two seasons under him.
Navy Midshipmen.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records 5.9 yards per play and 25 points per game allowed as the most since 2021.
Navy Midshipmen.tempo: Not addressed directly, though the guide notes the offensive scheme limits possessions.
Navy Midshipmen.run_pass: Heavily run-weighted by scheme. The guide adds an important methodological caution: Navy's defensive numbers must be read in the context of an offensive scheme that limits possessions.
Navy Midshipmen.personnel: Addressed through the Wing-T modified triple option.
Navy Midshipmen.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide identifies the specific gap it expects at the position: Blake Horvath's 58.8% completion rate trailed only Roger Staubach among Navy passers with at least 120 attempts, while Braxton Woodson is at 46.3% — though Woodson knows the scheme, having started games in each of the last two seasons, and averaged 9.4 yards per carry on 44 attempts.
Navy Midshipmen.continuity: Head coach and offensive coordinator return; the defensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 3, 0 and 0, plus 2 for 11 returning starters, totalling 9.
Navy Midshipmen.staff_turnover: Internal rather than external, and initiated by the head coach: Volker demoted, Lewis promoted, and Newberry taking back the play-calling.
Navy Midshipmen.vsin_assessment: Credit for the hire, with the attribution question left open. The guide credits Newberry for hiring Cronic, whose wrinkles gave Navy new life in the American, then poses the central question — whether the improvement was Cronic or a generational run of offensive leaders — with Horvath, Alex Tecza and all-time leading receiver Eli Heidenreich all gone. It grants the scheme creates productive players, then quantifies the hole: Navy is missing 93.5% of its passing yards, over 83% of its rushing yards and over 84% of its receiving yards. It calls the defensive question the million-dollar one.
Navy Midshipmen.strengths: A distinctive offensive scheme the guide says gives opponents much to prepare for, with a documented jump from 17.7 to over 31 points per game; offensive-coordinator continuity; a head coach taking back defensive play-calling in an area the guide calls his roots; five of the top seven tacklers back; and a quarterback who already knows the system.
Navy Midshipmen.concerns: The loss of 93.5% of passing yards, over 83% of rushing yards and over 84% of receiving yards; a quarterback whose completion rate is 46.3% against his predecessor's 58.8%; and defensive numbers at their worst since 2021 in a scheme context the guide says will only get harder as offensive production falls.
Navy Midshipmen.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

North Texas Eagles.previous_hc_experience: Extensive, and central to the assessment. The Coaching Carousel records that Neal Brown has over 120 games of head coaching experience, all at the FBS level, was very successful at Troy with three 10-win seasons in a row before heading to Morgantown, was let go from West Virginia in 2024, and served as Steve Sarkisian's assistant in 2025.
North Texas Eagles.oc: Neal Brown himself — the guide records he will call his own plays.
North Texas Eagles.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
North Texas Eagles.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
North Texas Eagles.play_caller: Neal Brown, explicitly — and the guide says this may work well or not at all.
North Texas Eagles.offensive_scheme: Addressed by contrast rather than by name. The Coaching Carousel says Brown is an offensive-minded coach, but not like Eric Morris, who ran more of a run-and-shoot style. The team pages qualify his record: Troy did not play with much tempo or light up scoreboards, though it scored 30-plus in each of his last three seasons, and West Virginia averaged 30-plus in only two of six.
North Texas Eagles.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
North Texas Eagles.tempo: Addressed as a tension. The guide notes Troy did not play with much tempo, while the athletic department had been willing to go high-octane and up-tempo with Morris, and allows Brown might reinvent himself or return to his Texas Tech approach.
North Texas Eagles.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
North Texas Eagles.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide notes Tayven Jackson steps down in class with his first non-Power Four team but has not taken great care of the football, and that he originally went to Tennessee and started games for Indiana and UCF.
North Texas Eagles.continuity: None. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator, 0 for the quarterback and 0 for 5 returning starters — a total of 0.
North Texas Eagles.staff_turnover: Complete, after Eric Morris left for Oklahoma State following what the guide calls probably the best season in programme history.
North Texas Eagles.prior_school: Troy, West Virginia, Texas Tech and Kentucky are the guide's reference points for Brown's coordinator and head-coaching work, with Texas the most recent. The West Virginia connection reaches the roster: Jahiem White averaged 6.5 yards per carry there and rejoins Brown. The guide also records Tayven Jackson from Tennessee by way of Indiana and UCF, and Aaron Alexander from Arkansas State.
North Texas Eagles.portal_recruiting: The entire roster, and the guide is unusually direct about its quality: beyond a few exceptions, most of these players simply did not latch on at their previous schools.
North Texas Eagles.vsin_assessment: Openly pessimistic, and the Carousel says so about itself. It records that Adam Burke would not call himself a glass-half-full person by nature but is often optimistic about new coaching hires — and cannot say that here. He allows it might work and that the bar isn't terribly high, given the programme has three winning seasons since 2013, but writes that it feels like North Texas is drifting closer to mediocrity again rather than living up to what should be their new standard. The team pages suggest the season's motto might be to smile that it happened rather than cry that it is over, call this possibly the most stripped-down programme they have seen, and state plainly that they still like the Under.
North Texas Eagles.strengths: Over 120 games of FBS head-coaching experience including three straight 10-win seasons at Troy, coordinator work at Troy, Texas Tech and Kentucky, a low bar given three winning seasons since 2013, and a handful of genuine transfer additions including a 6.5-yards-per-carry back who already played for him.
North Texas Eagles.concerns: A Stability Score of 0 with five returning starters and, by the guide's inventory, a top returning rusher with 95 yards, a top pass catcher with seven grabs, a top tackler with 32 stops and no returning kicker or punter; a play-calling arrangement the guide says may work well or not at all; a stylistic mismatch with what the athletic department had been backing; and institutional conditions the guide says show little investment.
North Texas Eagles.betting: The guide states its position plainly: with a projection of 5.81 wins, it still likes the Under. Its reasoning is largely about the coaching transition and the stripped-down roster.
North Texas Eagles.carousel_summary: Adam Burke opens by placing himself: he would not call himself a glass-half-full person by nature, but when it comes to new coaching hires he is often optimistic — and he cannot say that about North Texas's hire of Brown, who was let go from West Virginia in 2024 and served as Steve Sarkisian's assistant in 2025. He gives the record fairly: over 120 games of head coaching experience, all at the FBS level, and real success at Troy with three 10-win seasons in a row before heading to Morgantown. He then draws the stylistic contrast that matters here — Brown is an offensive-minded guy, but not like Eric Morris, who ran more of a run-and-shoot style. His conclusion is hedged but clear: it might work and the bar isn't terribly high, given the programme has three winning seasons since 2013, but it feels like UNT is drifting closer to mediocrity again rather than living up to what should be their new standard.

Rice Owls.previous_hc_experience: Yes, at a lower level. The guide records Scott Abell stepping up from FCS Davidson to take what it calls one of the most challenging jobs in FBS.
Rice Owls.dc: Jon Kay, the previous regime's linebackers coach, promoted to coordinator.
Rice Owls.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Rice Owls.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Rice Owls.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Rice Owls.offensive_scheme: Named and quantified. The guide identifies an option offense and supplies the schematic precedent from Abell's Davidson, where quarterbacks attempted only 152 passes in 11 games while the team ran 640 times for 3,720 yards, with quarterback Andrew Frazier third in both rushing attempts and yards. With Rice at 647 rushing attempts against 224 passes last season, it expects an even starker split.
Rice Owls.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records 6.3 yards per play and nearly 33 points allowed, the worst defensive effort since 2022.
Rice Owls.run_pass: Extremely run-weighted and expected to become more so — 647 rushing attempts against 224 passes last season, with the guide expecting a starker split still.
Rice Owls.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Jacurri Brown having spent two years each at Miami and UCF with only 148 passes thrown and more interceptions than touchdowns at nine to six, while running for 821 yards on 137 carries, and allows he could be a difference-maker as a better runner than Chase Jenkins.
Rice Owls.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 6 returning starters, totalling 10.
Rice Owls.staff_turnover: Not addressed for 2026. The guide's staffing observation is retrospective: it finds it a bit surprising that a new head coach would simply promote the previous regime's linebackers coach to coordinator, and says it did not really work.
Rice Owls.prior_school: Davidson for Abell. On the roster the guide records Jacurri Brown having been at Miami and UCF.
Rice Owls.portal_recruiting: The guide notes Abell brought in a decent number of Power Four transfers.
Rice Owls.vsin_assessment: The job rated as the hardest in the conference, with a distinct scheme-level doubt. The guide calls Rice one of the most challenging jobs in FBS and notes even last season's bowl came because others withdrew and Rice's Academic Progress Rate scores merited an opportunity. Its most specific criticism is conference-level: Rice is attempting its own version of the option in a league that already contains two service academies, which makes scheming easier for opposing defenses seeing similar core concepts and blocking — supported by 3.1 yards per carry against Navy, 2.4 against Memphis, 3.8 against UTSA, 3.4 against UAB and 3.8 against South Florida. It expects another tough year while noting Abell seems up for it.
Rice Owls.strengths: Full staff continuity in year two, a head coach the guide says seems up for the challenge, a decent number of Power Four transfers, and a quarterback it rates a better runner than his predecessor in a scheme built around that.
Rice Owls.concerns: The option approach being run in a conference that already contains two academies, which the guide says makes it easier to scheme against; the worst defensive effort since 2022 under a coordinator promoted from the previous regime; a -4 turnover margin with just seven takeaways despite a run-heavy approach; only six returning starters; and the top seven tacklers gone.
Rice Owls.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

South Florida Bulls.previous_hc_experience: None. The Coaching Carousel records that Brian Hartline was a star wide receiver for Ohio State from 2005-08, was on the staff in Columbus from 2017-25 and was the Buckeyes' OC or co-OC the last three seasons. The team pages note he has never coached anywhere else in college.
South Florida Bulls.oc: Tim Beck, coaching since the late 1980s, whose only head-coaching job was Coastal Carolina.
South Florida Bulls.dc: Josh Aldridge, in from conference rival East Carolina, in his second year calling plays.
South Florida Bulls.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
South Florida Bulls.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
South Florida Bulls.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name for the offense. The Coaching Carousel flags that Aldridge is just in his second year calling plays.
South Florida Bulls.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide's benchmark is the standard set under Alex Golesh: five teams averaged 40-plus points last season and South Florida was one, averaging 49 in American play.
South Florida Bulls.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but the guide advances a conference-level thesis to judge it: stopping the run is the key in the American because most teams run well or use run-heavy schemes, and while everybody allows passing yards and 60-plus completion percentages, the teams that stop the run position themselves to succeed. Aldridge's East Carolina unit allowed 3.6 yards per carry and South Florida allowed 3.7.
South Florida Bulls.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
South Florida Bulls.personnel: Not addressed in guide beyond the guide calling this a big front seven.
South Florida Bulls.qb_development: Addressed as recruitment rather than development. Hartline and Tim Beck added Michael Van Buren via Mississippi State and LSU, and Luke Kromenhoek via Florida State and Mississippi State, with the guide crediting Van Buren with genuine success including an 8-to-2 ratio at LSU last season across four starts and relief work.
South Florida Bulls.continuity: None. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator, 0 for the quarterback and 0 for 7 returning starters — a total of 0.
South Florida Bulls.staff_turnover: Complete, after Alex Golesh moved up to Auburn.
South Florida Bulls.prior_school: Ohio State for Hartline, and the Carousel treats the connection as his defining asset — he was directly responsible for Marvin Harrison Jr., Garrett Wilson, Emeka Egbuka, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Chris Olave, Carnell Tate and now Jeremiah Smith. East Carolina for Aldridge, where the guide notes he worked under Blake Harrell, whom it calls an outstanding defensive mind and good head coach. Coastal Carolina is Beck's head-coaching reference point.
South Florida Bulls.portal_recruiting: Rated highly in aggregate and doubted in detail. The guide notes most portal acquisitions did not play much previously, then supplies the counterweight: 247Sports graded South Florida's portal haul the best in the conference and 58th nationally with 44 commits — a lot of scouting and a lot of new faces. It frames the roster philosophy as highly touted recruits who did not make it dropping to a Group of Six programme to get back on the radar, most of them quarterbacks here.
South Florida Bulls.vsin_assessment: A recruiter of the highest order whose breadth the guide questions, with a coordinator split. The Coaching Carousel says December 3 was a day Ohio State fans had been dreading for a long time, calls the receiver pipeline just one attractive element, then states it is fair to question Hartline's experience outside of his offensive bubble, and adds that DC Josh Aldridge may be just as important while noting he is only in his second year calling plays. The team pages call Hartline the world's best wide receiver recruiter, state their reservation about Tim Beck openly — it took him 35 years to get a head job, Coastal Carolina did not go well at 20-18, and they personally find him underwhelming as a coordinator — and rate the Aldridge hire highly. Their real question is whether Hartline is a programme builder or thrived on a foundation already laid at Ohio State.
South Florida Bulls.strengths: A head coach the guide calls the world's best wide receiver recruiter with a documented NFL pipeline and three seasons as Ohio State's OC or co-OC, the best-graded portal haul in the conference at 44 commits, a defensive coordinator the guide rates highly from a unit that allowed 3.6 yards per carry, a big front seven, and a quarterback addition with an 8-to-2 ratio at LSU.
South Florida Bulls.concerns: A Stability Score of 0 with seven returning starters, a head coach who has never coached anywhere else in college and whose experience outside his offensive bubble both parts of the guide question, an offensive coordinator the guide says it personally finds underwhelming with a 20-18 head-coaching record, a defensive play-caller in only his second year, and a roster of players who mostly did not play much before.
South Florida Bulls.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.
South Florida Bulls.carousel_summary: Adam Burke frames the hire from Columbus outward: suffice it to say that December 3 was a day Ohio State fans had been dreading for a long time. He records that Hartline was a star wide receiver for the Buckeyes from 2005-08, was on the staff there from 2017-25, and was directly responsible for Marvin Harrison Jr., Garrett Wilson, Emeka Egbuka, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Chris Olave, Carnell Tate and now Jeremiah Smith — calling the absurd receiver pipeline just one attractive element, alongside his three seasons as Ohio State's OC or co-OC. He notes USF is looking to keep up the offensive prowess it had under another Ohio State alum in Alex Golesh, then states his reservation: it's fair to question Hartline's experience outside of his offensive bubble. He closes by naming a second decisive figure — just as important as Hartline might be DC Josh Aldridge, who is just in his second year calling plays.

Temple Owls.oc: Tyler Walker, the former Montana State coordinator.
Temple Owls.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Temple Owls.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Temple Owls.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Temple Owls.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records that with K.C. Keeler and Tyler Walker the offense improved by more than a touchdown per game.
Temple Owls.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, and the guide's key analytical point is that the defensive improvement was almost entirely turnover-driven, since most per-play and rate stats were not much better under Brian Smith — one of the nation's worst red zone defenses, below average on third down, and 30 plays of 30-plus yards allowed.
Temple Owls.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Temple Owls.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide characterises the departing starter's value precisely — Evan Simon made safe, reliable throws that did not generate much yardage, only 19 touchdown passes after six in the opener against UMass, but which protected the ball and gave an undermanned defense a better chance — and records virtually no experience behind him.
Temple Owls.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 10 returning starters, totalling 12.
Temple Owls.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Temple Owls.prior_school: Montana State for Tyler Walker. On the roster the guide records Jaxon Smolik from Penn State and Ajani Sheppard from Rutgers by way of Washington State.
Temple Owls.portal_recruiting: Addressed indirectly — the guide reads Temple's late-season yardage collapse as a major depth problem the staff has possibly addressed.
Temple Owls.vsin_assessment: The best of three first-year peers in the present tense, but with the gains attributed to something unlikely to repeat. The guide judges Rice and Florida Atlantic made progress toward the future while Temple may have done best in the present, records the offense improving by more than a touchdown per game under Keeler and Walker, and notes that even a +11 turnover margin could not produce enough upsets to end the bowl drought. Its decisive argument is stated as such: Keeler could not reach six wins with a +11 turnover margin last season, and this group looks worse at the most important position. It supplies the context for the turnover swing — Temple was -10, -20 and -11 under Stan Drayton.
Temple Owls.strengths: Full staff continuity in year two, an offense that improved by more than a touchdown per game, a first positive turnover margin in some time, three of the top four tacklers returning, and a late-season depth problem the guide says may have been addressed.
Temple Owls.concerns: A quarterback room with virtually no experience after losing a 25-to-2 starter and his backup, 16 sacks generated while allowing over six yards per play, defensive gains the guide says were almost entirely turnover-driven, and a -624 yardage margin including -854 across the last four games.
Temple Owls.betting: The guide's argument is explicitly about the head coach's ceiling under favourable conditions: Keeler could not reach six wins with a +11 turnover margin last season, and this group looks worse at the most important position. Projection is 5.33 wins.
